speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you're here regarding a rash and some recent health changes; can you tell me exactly where the rash started and how long it has been present?

Also, have you noticed any accompanying symptoms like fever, joint pain, or difficulty breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant development; seeing a primary care provider for arthritis and a new cough alongside a sudden rash suggests a systemic issue rather than a simple skin allergy. Could you describe the specific appearance of the rash, does it itch, and have you noticed any joint swelling or shortness of breath? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count; REQUEST IMAGES: [Skin_Rash_Photos]

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: Normal, Hemoglobin: Normal, Platelets: Normal; IMAGES: Skin_Rash_Photos: Coalescing erythematous macules, bullae, desquamation noted localized to the upper half of the back; Ulcers and erythema present in oropharynx.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). The combination of recent medication initiation for arthritis, oral ulcers, and the specific skin findings of coalescing bullae and desquamation on the upper back is highly indicative of this severe mucocutaneous reaction.
